Complete guide to Pokémon Emerald. Walkthrough, gym leaders, Battle Frontier, best team, and tips for completing the Hoenn Pokédex.

Pokémon Emerald is the enhanced remake of Ruby and Sapphire, released for the Game Boy Advance in 2004. It features updated graphics, new story elements, and the legendary Battle Frontier. This complete guide covers everything you need to master Pokémon Emerald.

Table of Contents

  1. Choosing Your Starter
  2. Main Story Walkthrough
  3. Gym Leaders Guide
  4. Battle Frontier Guide
  5. Best Team for Emerald

Choosing Your Starter

The three starters in Pokémon Emerald are Treecko (Grass), Torchic (Fire), and Mudkip (Water). Mudkip is widely considered the best starter for Emerald because it evolves into Swampert, which has only one weakness (Grass) and excellent stats. Torchic is also strong once it evolves into Blaziken, but struggles against the early gyms. Treecko is the hardest to use but becomes powerful late game.

Main Story Walkthrough

The story of Pokémon Emerald follows the Hoenn journey with significant additions over Ruby and Sapphire. Both Team Magma and Team Aqua are active antagonists, and Rayquaza plays a central role in the plot. The climax involves Rayquaza descending to stop the battle between Groudon and Kyogre at Sootopolis City.

Key story beats include: getting your starter from Professor Birch, challenging the eight gym leaders, dealing with Team Magma and Team Aqua, awakening Rayquaza at Sky Pillar, and challenging the Elite Four. After becoming Champion, the Battle Frontier becomes available.

Gym Leaders Guide

Emerald features eight gym leaders, each specializing in a different type. The gym leaders are slightly different from Ruby and Sapphire, with updated teams and rematches available after the main story.

  • Roxanne (Rock): Geodude and Nosepass. Use Water or Grass moves.
  • Brawly (Fighting): Machop and Makuhita. Use Flying or Psychic moves.
  • Wattson (Electric): Voltorb, Electrike, and Magneton. Use Ground moves.
  • Flannery (Fire): Numel, Slugma, and Torkoal. Use Water or Rock moves.
  • Norman (Normal): Slaking, Spinda, Vigoroth, and Linoone. Use Fighting moves.
  • Winona (Flying): Swablu, Tropius, Pelipper, Skarmory, and Altaria. Use Electric or Ice moves.
  • Tate and Liza (Psychic): Solrock and Lunatone. Use Dark, Ghost, or Bug moves.
  • Wallace (Water): Luvdisc, Whiscash, Sealeo, Seaking, and Milotic. Use Electric or Grass moves.

Battle Frontier Guide

The Battle Frontier is the defining feature of Pokémon Emerald. It is a post-game area with seven unique battle facilities, each with its own rules and challenges. Winning battles earns Battle Points (BP), which can be exchanged for rare items and TMs.

The seven facilities are: Battle Tower, Battle Dome, Battle Palace, Battle Arena, Battle Factory, Battle Pike, and Battle Pyramid. Each facility is led by a Frontier Brain, who can be challenged after winning a certain number of consecutive battles. Defeating a Frontier Brain earns a Symbol, which is a prestigious achievement.

Best Team for Emerald

A well-balanced team for Pokémon Emerald should cover the gyms and the Battle Frontier:

  • Swampert: Water/Ground, excellent bulk and only one weakness.
  • Gardevoir: Psychic, powerful special attacker with good coverage.
  • Manectric: Electric, fast special attacker for Water and Flying types.
  • Slaking: Normal, incredible Attack and HP despite Truant ability.
  • Torkoal or Camerupt: Fire type for Steel and Grass coverage.
  • Altaria or Salamence: Dragon/Flying for late-game power.
